title: Pleasure without a verdict on expectations
meaning: Uneasy expectations can obstruct shared pleasure when the actual experience is immediately subjected to a strict assessment.
text: You can choose a shared pleasure reasonably and still wonder whether it is allowed simply to delight you. Justice in the physical position of Svadhisthana suggests matching leisure to agreements: a clear price, a fair turn and both people's wishes considered. The Moon in energy leans towards uncertain expectations and fearing disappointment before experience begins. Justice in emotions checks the result: was it worth the effort, and did everyone receive an equal share? One appearance guides the choice; the other conducts its inner assessment.

Suppose you choose an unfamiliar dessert to share. Before ordering, you worry about the taste; afterwards, you try to decide whether the whole purchase was justified. **Pleasure becomes cramped when it must immediately justify itself.** Between expectation and judgement, the taste, each other's amused reactions and the chance to try something unfamiliar can pass unnoticed. Even a mixed impression can remain a pleasant shared episode without earning a unanimous positive verdict.

The difficulty is answering uncertainty with more exact calculation. You check reviews, compare terms and divide pleasure into equal portions beforehand, yet an uneasy guess still finds room. Fairness helps with the conditions, while feeling does not always submit to arithmetic. Shared leisure benefits from permission to be an interesting experience without a final ruling on its overall value.
